headline_hook: OpenAI Goes Physical While GPT-5.5 Tops the Hardest Coding Benchmark

pick_of_the_day.thesis: A 5B-parameter open-source model trained on 27K hours of real robot data proves the sim-to-real gap is a data problem, not a scale problem — and that reshapes who gets to build useful robots.

model_literacy.relevance: With OpenAI hiring for physical AI and τ0-WM releasing a unified video-action model, today's news hinges on world models — neural networks that predict how the physical world changes in response to actions, bridging perception and control in a single architecture.

items.title: OpenAI Is Building Robots — and Hiring the Team to Do It
items.angle: Sam Altman formally enters the physical-AI race, signaling OpenAI sees embodiment as a core frontier alongside language and reasoning
items.key_fact: Hiring across full-stack hardware, ops, systems, and ML for robot manufacturing

items.title: τ0-WM: A 5B Open-Source World Model Trained on 27K Hours of Real Robots
items.angle: The largest open-source robotic foundation model to date unifies video generation and action control — a template for how the robotics field catches up to language models
items.key_fact: 5B parameters, 27,300 hours of real-robot teleoperation and egocentric video data

items.title: GPT-5.5 Hits 70% on DeepSWE — at Half the Cost and Speed of Opus 4.8
items.angle: The first hard benchmark where OpenAI decisively leads on long-horizon coding, and the efficiency gap matters more than the accuracy gap
items.key_fact: 70% pass@1 vs 58% for Opus 4.8, using ~3x fewer tokens at half the cost and wall-clock time

items.title: ChatGPT for Google Sheets Can Be Exploited to Steal Your Data
items.angle: PromptArmor shows that every LLM tool integration is an attack surface — and the most popular ones are shipping faster than they're being secured
items.key_fact: Data exfiltration and phishing demonstrated in the widely-used ChatGPT Google Sheets plugin

items.title: Codegraph: Pre-Indexed Knowledge Graphs That Cut Agent Token Burn
items.angle: A codebase indexer that works with every major AI coding agent — fewer tokens, fewer tool calls, 100% local
items.key_fact: 34,000+ GitHub stars; compatible with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini

items.title: Codex Desktop Quietly Killed Its Most-Used Power Feature
items.angle: Simon Willison flags the silent removal of 'Copy as Markdown' transcript export — a cautionary tale about shipping fast and breaking power-user trust
items.key_fact: Willison called transcript export his single most-used Codex capability

items.title: SoftBank Bets €75 Billion on French AI Infrastructure
items.angle: The largest single AI infrastructure commitment in European history turns the compute buildout into an explicitly geopolitical race
items.key_fact: Up to €75B for 5GW of data center capacity in France

items.title: Simon Willison Says He's Retiring From Tech to Live Offline
items.angle: Whether sincere or satirical, when the AI developer community's most prolific voice walks away, it's worth asking what he saw
items.key_fact: Willison shaped how an entire generation of developers thinks about LLM tooling

items.title: Willison Considers Cancelling His AI Subscription — and That's the Point
items.angle: When someone this deep in the ecosystem questions the value proposition, it reveals the gap between AI capability and AI utility for power users
items.key_fact: Published one day after his retirement post, creating an intentional narrative arc

items.title: 1.5 Billion Chinese Users Are Quietly Winning the Open-Source AI Race
items.angle: A contrarian argument that the West's obsession with closed-model scaling is blinding it to the open-source ecosystem being battle-tested at nation-scale
items.key_fact: 1.5 billion users actively improving open-source models in China

items.title: What If Remote Work, Not AI, Broke Junior Hiring?
items.angle: FT's counter-narrative argues the junior hiring crisis is a mentorship and on-ramp problem, not an automation one
items.key_fact: FT front-page analysis attributing weak junior pipelines to remote work's erosion of in-person mentorship

items.title: Mollick: The Future Isn't Autonomous Agents — It's Agents That Ask Better Questions
items.angle: A practical framework for agent UX design: the real unlock is knowing when to interrupt, not when to keep going
items.key_fact: Argues agents should interrupt when stuck, uncertain, or facing consequential decisions

items.title: Run Full Python Web Apps in the Browser — No Server Required
items.angle: Pyodide + service workers let you ship ASGI apps entirely client-side, opening the door to zero-infrastructure AI demos
items.key_fact: Full Python ASGI framework running in-browser via Pyodide and service workers

items.title: TradingView + Claude MCP: Autonomous Chart Analysis in 5 Minutes
items.angle: A viral demo showing MCP's potential beyond code editors — a Claude agent drawing technical analysis on live trading charts
items.key_fact: 5 minutes from setup to autonomous chart annotation using TradingView's MCP server

quick_links.title: Odysseus: Self-Hosted AI Workspace for Privacy-First Teams
quick_links.angle: Another entry in the growing self-hosted ChatGPT alternative space
quick_links.key_fact: Hit the HN front page; no data leaves your infrastructure

quick_links.title: Flutter Gets Its First AI-Native Debugging MCP Server
quick_links.angle: First dedicated mobile-framework MCP server to gain real traction
quick_links.key_fact: Real-time debug, profile, and optimize running Flutter apps via AI agents

quick_links.title: The New Economics of Prototyping in the AI Era
quick_links.angle: Practitioner argues AI compressed prototyping from days to hours, changing what's worth building
quick_links.key_fact: Front-page HN discussion on compressed experimentation cycles

quick_links.title: Forward Deployed Engineers: The Role Everyone Will Hire Next Quarter
quick_links.angle: Latent Space highlights the new hybrid role bridging AI capability and customer deployment
quick_links.key_fact: Emerging job archetype at the intersection of ML engineering and field engineering

quick_links.title: Open Envelope: A Standard Schema for Multi-Agent Teams
quick_links.angle: Early-stage open standard for how agents discover each other and hand off tasks
quick_links.key_fact: Addresses the gap: no standard way to describe agent team compositions

quick_links.title: AI Interview Codex: The Open-Source ML/AI Interview Prep Guide
quick_links.angle: Comprehensive repo with notebooks and study plans for the current AI engineer hiring wave
quick_links.key_fact: Covers ML coding, system design, LLM/GenAI, DSA, and MLOps prep
